title: Moving to local llm
author: Xpberb
selftext:
Has anybody found a decent local only workflow that's decent? Kinda tired of nuking credits and I have some decent GPUs..

Currently CODEX > blender/unity MCP mainly.

I know Ollama could help some but feel I need to build the front end somehow to deal with it better like I do codex

comments.author: Charming_You_25
comments.body: The qwen model is decent. I’d use it for testing and scouting. Have it run off a queue so you don’t need to wait for it (it’s slow but usably good).

replies.author: Xpberb
replies.body: What do you use as the front end orchestrator? Ollama UI itself?

replies.author: Ok-File-2759
replies.body: If you’re asking about what agent harness to use, there’s a lot. The most popular ones right now seem to be the Hermes agent, DeepSeek harness, and OpenCode. All of those allow you to hookup multiple different models from multiple different companies

replies.author: Charming_You_25
replies.body:
Your question doesn’t make sense. I use opencode, Claude with a cliapiproxy (which can run any model), and openclaw all for different purposes. My local model that hang out and occasionally wakes up and does some things for me runs as an openclaw automation. Though for cheap and fast i use deepseek non-locally. When im orchestrating a lot of stuff i typically use a frontier model, though my orchestration patterns have changed a lot to take into account frontier model cache invalidation and now i dont have an orchestrator sitting around waiting and responding to everything a small model does. Frontier model sends off batches of fixes to other frontier models, and I set a timer for 28m to have it check in. When it’s done I send off batches of browser testers, sleep it for 28m again, and have it check later.

A small model like qwen you could use it locally also with opencode, have it perform reconnaissance like where in the codebase this bug is, then have a better model actually fix it, then have small model perform browser tests to verify.

comments.author: drunnells
comments.body: On Nvidia P40s, I use Qwen 3.8 27b with Hermes or opencode or openwebui. I far prefer the results of Codex/Astra, but Qwen and Hermes can do some stuff.

comments.author: Awkward_Education704
comments.body: I have played around a bit and I find that coding is much better with CODEX but I use image generation with qwen image and then use Trellis2 and Pixal3d to turn the images to 3d models using ComfyUI. The models aren't the best but are a good start and saves a lot on credits

replies.author: Xpberb
replies.body: Qwen good for animation QA and improvement? Just stuck in the long animation/art QA process.

comments.author: Upstairs-Mulberry365
comments.body: There are no good enough local models that you run locally, at least in my experience.

comments.author: reality_comes
comments.body:
I havent had great success doing anything advanced in blender with the MCP locally. You can do some low poly stuff though. 

Try Qwen 3.8 27b
